hypothesis: Admit and receipt the terminal oracle-scored trajectories without scheduling the ten post-budget SAC updates that cannot affect another proposal, then consume the already queued stop and execute the existing shutdown before the evaluator grace expires, while preserving every learning update that influences later fragment decisions.
method_thesis: Decompose the allowed unlabeled corpus into a fixed vocabulary of chemically sanitized, attachment-labelled fragments and use its reconstruction trajectories only to behavior-clone a task-agnostic graph policy. In each independent objective session, start complete constructions from a sampled vocabulary fragment and repeatedly sample a three-part categorical action: an open attachment site on the current partial graph, a fragment, and a compatible attachment site on that fragment, with an explicit stop action and valence-checked transitions. Canonicalize completed graphs and submit only fresh valid unique assemblies in the evaluator-announced batch; the vocabulary is a combinatorial action alphabet, not a pool of whole-molecule candidates. Put the scored initial molecules when representable and every subsequently generated trajectory into a task-local replay buffer, assign the observed oracle score only at the terminal transition, and update corrected twin soft-Q critics, the stochastic actor, and its entropy temperature from uniformly replayed transitions. The next molecules are sampled directly from the updated actor, so no corpus molecule is retrieved, ranked, or screened and no finite molecular candidate set is enumerated. Off-policy trajectory reuse lets each scarce terminal observation train many partial-graph decisions, while maximum-entropy action sampling resists early policy collapse; both serve the sole benchmark target of a stronger final Top-1 on each session.

Require zero post-budget SAC updates, both receipts, and exit within the evaluator's five-second grace while every earlier feedback boundary retains ten SAC updates.

applicability_conditions: The repair applies only to the terminal observe message whose budget_remaining is zero and which the evaluator immediately follows with stop; no later suggestion can consume learning performed from that feedback.

Final accepted and rejected entries remain admitted through the existing observe path and its oracle-trajectory receipt, while all feedback boundaries that can affect a later suggestion retain the unchanged ten SAC updates.

The repair does not change preparation, fragment construction, validity masks, replay selection, critic or actor objectives, entropy-temperature adjustment, novelty filtering, batch sizing, or any proposal emitted before budget exhaustion.
research_intent.falsifier: The repair is falsified if terminal budget-zero feedback starts any SAC replay update, fails to emit the final oracle-trajectory or shutdown receipt, or any formal task still fails to exit within the five-second stop grace; it is also falsified if a nonterminal feedback boundary performs other than the unchanged ten updates.
research_intent.implementation_change: Add an optional update-count keyword to FragmentSoftActorCritic.observe and pass it unchanged to the existing train_sac call. In run, compute whether the received observe message exhausts the budget and pass zero updates only for that terminal feedback, otherwise pass the existing SAC_UPDATES_PER_FEEDBACK value of ten; retain the existing final-feedback admission, stop validation, and shutdown path without changing any algorithmic calculation.

research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Algorithm Node n-a5a9c7e8871a consumed all 300 oracle calls on each of five seed-0 objectives but returned no formal score because run synchronously entered ten SAC updates after the final budget-zero observe before reading the evaluator's queued stop. Every task log ends inside that final update block without a final oracle-trajectory receipt or shutdown receipt, and every task is recorded as BUGGY with 'candidate did not exit after stop'.

applicability_conditions: The repair is directly supported for all five recorded seed-0 Objective Sessions under the frozen profile of 300 oracle calls, ten suggestions per batch, and a five-second post-stop grace: every session admitted its terminal feedback, emitted both required receipts, and exited cleanly.

The terminal branch is supported when an observe message reports budget_remaining less than or equal to zero and the evaluator immediately sends stop, exactly as evaluate.py does in this benchmark. No later proposal can consume an update from that feedback.

Terminal admission remains operational before training suppression: the five batch-29 receipts account for 50 accepted trajectories, 419 inserted transitions, 50 terminal reward assignments, zero nonterminal nonzero rewards, and zero observed rejections. Terminal rejected-entry behavior was not exercised in this replica.

Every feedback boundary capable of affecting a later proposal retained the inherited schedule: all 140 batch-1-through-28 receipts report ten updates, with 1,400 replay/critic events and 700 actor events across the five sessions.

Causal isolation is strong for this recovery. Prepared-artifact content is identical, each Candidate trajectory is byte-identical to its Parent trajectory, and every task log is byte-identical through terminal provenance; the evidence therefore supports unchanged preparation, construction, masks, replay selection, SAC objectives, novelty filtering, batch sizing, and emitted proposals before budget exhaustion.

The result establishes operational completion on screening seed 0, not independent-seed reliability, a precise exit-latency distribution, or transfer to a different evaluator stop protocol, batch size, model scale, replay scale, or shutdown workload.

Because evaluate.py sends stop and then finish_after_stop enforces benchmark_tasks.json's five-second grace, each Parent stop-to-clean-exit latency was at least the five-second timeout and no clean exit was observed; the evaluator does not record a more precise elapsed value.
observable_measurements.value: For node n-ccfe8deb016a, every one of the five terminal batch-29 feedback paths has zero fragment_sac_uniform_replay_draw events, zero fragment_sac_twin_soft_bellman_update events, zero fragment_sac_actor_temperature_update events, and zero fragment_sac_activation_observables events after the final ten provenance records. Instead, line 1078 of every task log is fragment_sac_oracle_trajectory_replay with training.updates=0 and training.actor_updates=0, and line 1079 is fragment_sac_shutdown. The five final receipts admit all 50/50 accepted terminal trajectories exactly once, assign 50 terminal rewards and zero nonterminal nonzero rewards, and add 419 transitions; no terminal evaluator rejection occurred. Every earlier batch-1-through-28 receipt on every task reports training.updates=10, giving 140/140 preserved nonterminal feedback boundaries, 1,400 replay/critic updates, and 700 actor updates. All five task summaries are status ok at 300 oracle calls and the seed summary is status ok at 1,500 calls. The evaluator does not timestamp stop and process exit separately, so exact latency is unavailable, but its successful finish_after_stop call proves that every candidate exited cleanly within the enforced five-second grace. Thus the observable decreased from Parent terminal SAC work plus a stop timeout to zero terminal SAC updates plus an exit within grace. The Candidate and Parent trajectory files are byte-identical for every task, and their task logs are byte-identical through the final provenance line 1077, showing that no earlier proposal or feedback update changed.
